subject: Post-call: burst/tail behavior + concurrency checkpoints (FastLane pilot)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.inference>
To: Caroline Moss <caroline@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2028 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: burst/tail behavior + concurrency checkpoints (FastLane pilot)

Thanks for taking the time today, Caroline — good conversation. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into pilot planning.

Summary of what we heard from FastLane on the call:
- Bursts: 8–12 requests over ~6–12s windows, typically triggered by batch job fan-in or user onboarding spikes.
- Per-request token payload: usually 700–1,200 tokens (prompt + history).
- Streaming: enabled for the majority of endpoints; client uses 200–300 token chunking.
- Target SLOs discussed: p95 latency target for first meaningful token ~250–300ms (you mentioned 300ms as acceptable but prefer 250ms if possible).

What Redwood needs to size/qualify: (please confirm these items)
1) Typical steady-state QPS and tokens/sec across one 5-minute window (not peak)
2) Peak window profile (burst duration, QPS during burst, tokens/sec during burst) — give 1, 10, and 60s windows if possible
3) Concurrency distribution (how many concurrent streaming connections during a peak?)
4) Any strict TLS/KMS/VPC constraints for Private deployment pilot (affects routing and fallback)

Attachments: call-recording.txt (notes), raw-sample-trace.csv (anonymized traces sample) — see attached stubs.

Recommended immediate next steps (my proposal):
- Caroline: share a 24‑hour sample trace (csv) and 7‑day peak/steady summary by EOD Wed (7/11).
- Redwood (Sean + Marissa): produce two sizing proposals by Fri (7/13): conservative (reserve for 99th percentile bursts) and cost-optimized (accept graceful degradation above configured thresholds).
- Follow-up call: 30 minutes next week to walk sizing options and tradeoffs. I propose Tue/Wed 8–11am PT; please share availability.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Sean/Marissa and we’ll produce the draft math + AMI configuration matrix.

—
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Caroline Moss <caroline@fastlane.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.inference>
Cc: FastLane Engineering <eng+infra@fastlane.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: burst/tail behavior + concurrency checkpoints (FastLane pilot)

Thanks, Aisha — helpful recap. A couple clarifications and a quick data drop so you can start the sizing math: we ran through a few sessions internally and pulled these numbers from last week's production logs.

Current quick metrics (UTC timestamps converted):
- Typical steady-state: 2.5 QPS across our inference endpoint (mostly background orchestrator calls) ~ 1,900 tokens/sec total.
- Short bursts (seen ~3x/day): 9–11 QPS sustained for ~8–14s; average token payload ~950 tokens, so peak token/sec spikes to ~10,500–11,000.
- Extended peaks (rare): up to 22 QPS for 30–45s during batch opens; token/sec ~20k–25k in those windows.
- Concurrent streaming connections during short bursts: 60–120 concurrent clients (connections multiplexed; many clients stream).

SLO nuance: our product team said they care most about first‑token latency for interactive flows (web console + mobile). Background batch consumers can tolerate a higher lag (we'd route them to lower-cost variants). So if Redwood can show a plan to hold first-token p95 to ~275ms under short bursts (and outline fallback behavior for extended peaks), we'll be in good shape.

I've attached an anonymized 2‑hour sample trace (raw-sample-trace.csv) — it includes per-request token counts, timestamps, and a short event type field.

Questions for your sizing doc: does Redwood want sample traces in any particular schema? We can convert if helpful. Also, are there recommended limits on streaming chunk size we should enforce on the client side to reduce tail amplification?

Happy to hop on a follow-up once you and Sean have a draft.

—
Caroline Moss
Head of Product, FastLane
caroline@fastlane.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2028 01:28:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FastLane quick-capacity sketch (for Aisha to send)

Internal notes — quick back-of-envelope sizing based on Caroline's numbers above. Attaching capacity-math.md stub for the full calc.

Assumptions taken from Caroline: peak short burst tokens/sec ~11k, extended peaks ~25k. Target first-token p95 ~275ms for interactive traffic.

Rough options:
- Conservative (SLA-forward): configure dedicated cluster to sustain 25k tokens/sec with safe headroom; target 275ms p95 -> recommend rtx-large instances (8xA100-equivalent) with persistent KV cache warming + 4x concurrency per GPU for streaming. Expected committed monthly cost: HIGH (estimate attached).
- Cost-optimized (graceful degrade): provision for 12k sustained tokens/sec; allow fallback to lighter variants and soft-queueing beyond that threshold. Target p95 <=300ms under intended steady+short bursts. Lower committed cost, but requires client-side retry/backoff guidance.

Open items for Aisha to confirm with FastLane:
1) Exact percent of traffic that is interactive vs batch (we used 60/40 split as placeholder).
2) Whether the product team is willing to accept model-variant fallback for 1–3% of requests during extended peaks.
3) Any hard limits on outbound network egress (affects Private deployment placement).

Action: I'll draft the two proposal decks (conservative vs cost-optimized) and a short appendix on streaming chunk sizing and KV-cache priming. Deliverable by Fri (7/13).

—
Sean Gallagher
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.inference>
To: Caroline Moss <caroline@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: burst/tail behavior + concurrency checkpoints (FastLane pilot)

Caroline — thanks for the trace and clarifications. Sean and I sketched two options (conservative vs cost-optimized) and an internal appendix on streaming chunk guidance. Next steps and owners below:

1) FastLane: confirm interactive vs batch split (Aisha) — action: Caroline — due Thu (7/11) EOD PT.
2) Redwood: deliver two sizing proposals + capacity math + pilot runbook — action: Sean/Marissa — due Fri (7/13) EOD PT.
3) FastLane & Redwood: 30-minute review call to walk the proposals and agree on pilot SLA/fallbacks — propose Tue 7/16 9:30–10:00am PT or Wed 7/17 10:00–10:30am PT. Please confirm preferred slot.

Notes on streaming chunk sizes: Sean recommends we test client-side chunk sizes of 128 and 256 tokens during the pilot; 512 tends to amplify tail in our experience. We'll include microbenchmarks in the pilot runbook.

I attached the sample trace and our internal capacity math stub. If you want, we can also run a short spike test using Redwood sandbox the week of 7/15 to validate tail behavior (requires a short traffic replay).

Let me know preferred call slot and I’ll send an invite + draft agenda.

Thanks —
Aisha
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Aisha@redwood.inference
